findings.desc: codex-cli-audit-r1 verified high: CLI still resolves LATTICE_AUTHORITY_CUSTOMER_API_KEY_PATH from a parsed trust env against consumer cwd instead of the trust env file directory. Server B-42a2 emits CUSTOMER_API_KEY_PATH="./lattice_staging-client.env" in lattice_authority_trust.env, so consuming an operator/server bundle by absolute LATTICE_AUTHORITY_TRUST_ENV_FILE from another cwd loads the trust env but fails to read the raw sidecar. Source: authority-client.ts lines 1541-1551 read the trust file path but only return env/path; lines 1616-1623 resolve trustPath via resolvePath(cwd, trustPath). Repro command: node --input-type=module minimal script importing dist/core/authority-client.js with trust env in a temp bundle and cwd in a different temp dir returned trustLoaded=true, urlSource=authority_trust_env, keySource=none, valuePresent=false, resolvedPathSuffix=authority-consumer-cwd-*/lattice_staging-client.env. Existing smokes only cover absolute sidecar path or cwd=bundleRoot, so the server-generated relative sidecar contract is not actually preserved.

codex-cli-audit-r2 verified high security/path-safety blocker: a server-provided trust env with LATTICE_AUTHORITY_CUSTOMER_API_KEY_PATH=./lattice_staging-client.env is resolved against the consumer cwd, so the CLI can read an unrelated same-named sidecar from cwd instead of the bundle sidecar. Source: authority-client.ts lines 1541-1551 keep only parsed trust env/path, and lines 1619-1623 call resolvePath(cwd, trustPath). Repro command imported dist/core/authority-client.js, wrote bundleRoot/lattice_authority_trust.env plus bundleRoot/lattice_staging-client.env and a different consumerRoot/lattice_staging-client.env, then called resolveAuthorityCustomerApiKey with cwd=consumerRoot; output was source=authority_trust_env, valueMatchesBundle=false, valueMatchesCwd=true, resolvedPathSuffix=authority-consumer-cwd-*/lattice_staging-client.env. This is a verified wrong-secret binding risk even though stdout remains clean and public generation helpers were removed.
